children: announced on Saturday that Icotyde, its FDA-approved therapy marketed with Protagonist Therapeutics
for plaque psoriasis, succeeded in a late-stage trial for psoriatic arthritis.

With studies showing that up to 30% of patients with plaque PsO also develop PsA, the positive outcome of the company’s Phase 3 ICONIC-PsA 1 represents another medical use for the interleukin-23 receptor antagonist.
In March, the FDA licensed Icotyde for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in those aged 12 years and older at a time when additional trials, including ICONIC-PsA 1 for the once-daily
At a rheumatology event on Saturday, J&J

said that ICONIC-PsA 1 met its primary endpoint, with 58% of patients on Icotyde at Week 16 achieving an American College of Rheumatology 20 (ACR20) response, which indicates 20% or more improvement in disease activity.
In comparison, 41% on placebo achieved ACR20. 29% and 13% also achieved ACR50 and ACR70, indicating ≥50% and ≥70% improvement, respectively, compared with 16% and 5% over the same period.
There were no new safety signals associated with Icotyde, with the treatment showing a tolerability profile consistent with its established safety profile, according to J&J
. The randomized trial enrolled biologic-naïve adults with active psoriatic arthritis.
